title: Pacific Islands Forum 2026: What Lowy’s Pacific team will be watching
gist: Ahead of the 55th Pacific Islands Forum in Palau (31 Aug–4 Sept 2026), Lowy analysts flag that the region's consensus-based 'Pacific Way' is straining under China pressure, El Niño shocks and a fuel crisis, with Taiwan readmitted, deep-sea mining, a Pacific security pact and the untested Pacific Resilience Facility all on the table.

insights.claim: After China's ballistic missile test splashed down in the Pacific, PIF foreign ministers failed to agree a joint statement at their August Suva meeting, softening language, not naming China directly, and deferring resolution to the Leaders' Statement in Palau.
insights.speaker: Oliver Nobetau
insights.so_what: Watch the Palau Leaders' Statement for whether the Forum can name China at all — a stalemate signals the limits of Pacific collective bargaining against Beijing.
insights.quote: foreign ministers failed to agree a joint statement
insights.locator: Oliver Nobetau, Director Pacific Islands Program

insights.claim: A Lowy director argues the consensus-based 'Pacific Way' may have reached its practical limits and that some contested matters are better left to individual sovereign choice than forced into a consensus that does not exist.
insights.speaker: Oliver Nobetau
insights.so_what: A shift away from consensus toward bilateral/sovereign action would fragment how external powers (China, Australia, US) must engage the region.
insights.quote: it may be time to be candid about the practical limits of regionalism

insights.claim: The Forum of 18 leaders will be chaired by Palau President Surangel Whipps Jr, who is pushing a tangible plan of action rather than more joint political statements as a central theme of the 2026 talks.
insights.speaker: Oliver Nobetau
insights.so_what: Palau's chairmanship sets the agenda; its pro-Taiwan, anti-mining stance shapes the odds of any China-favourable outcome.
insights.locator: A forum of 18 leaders needs decisive leadership

insights.claim: El Niño is already hitting the Pacific unevenly — some countries have declared drought while others are being rained out, and PNG faces extraordinary frosts worsening food security and clean water access.
insights.speaker: Oliver Nobetau
insights.so_what: Compounding climate shocks raise the region's demand for external food, water and disaster finance — a driver of aid and commodity flows.
insights.locator: The region is already feeling the pinch of El Niño

insights.claim: Closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran war caused fuel shortages and surging costs that exposed the Pacific's dependence on imported fossil fuel, reviving Whipps Jr's proposal for a 100% renewable energy transition and calls for a Pacific Energy Commissioner.
insights.speaker: Oliver Nobetau
insights.so_what: Energy-security pain is accelerating Pacific renewable ambition — a tailwind for regional clean-energy financing and infrastructure demand.
insights.quote: Shortages and surging fuel costs due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz have highlighted the Pacific dependence on imported fossil fuel
insights.locator: Sarah Thompson, Project Director Aus-PNG Network

insights.claim: The Pacific Resilience Facility, a Pacific-owned and managed climate fund designed to fill gaps left by hard-to-access global funds, will begin its first real test in Palau as leaders call for pilot project proposals.
insights.speaker: Oliver Nobetau
insights.so_what: Whether a locally-owned fund can deliver where global climate funds failed is a live test of regional financial self-reliance worth tracking for aid architecture.
insights.quote: can it deliver where global efforts have previously failed the Pacific?

insights.claim: Taiwan will rejoin the PIF Leaders Meeting as a development partner after being excluded from the 2024 Solomon Islands meeting under Beijing pressure, with host Palau wielding the same host power to welcome Taiwan back in defiance of China.
insights.speaker: Oliver Nobetau
insights.so_what: The host's discretion over Taiwan's status shows Pacific summitry as a swing venue in cross-Strait diplomacy year to year.
insights.quote: this year, the same power is being wielded to welcome Taiwan back in defiance of pressure from Beijing

insights.claim: Palau President Whipps Jr has publicly accused Beijing of coercion and complained of unwelcome Chinese maritime incursions into Palau's waters; Palau is one of only three Pacific nations with diplomatic ties to Taiwan.
insights.speaker: Oliver Nobetau
insights.so_what: Overt friction between the Forum host and Beijing lowers the odds of a China-accommodating consensus this cycle.
insights.locator: Whipps Jr has recently voiced his discontent

insights.claim: Solomon Islands PM Matthew Wale is championing a Pacific-wide security agreement that Australia has shown interest in, but Australia is warned not to overplay enthusiasm before wider Pacific buy-in lest it again be accused of putting geopolitical ambition ahead of local priorities.
insights.speaker: Oliver Nobetau
insights.so_what: A regional security pact's shape determines how much room Australia versus China has to embed in Pacific security — watch Australia's messaging discipline.
insights.locator: Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale

insights.claim: Commercial deep-sea mining is framed as an existential challenge to the Forum, pitting environment against economy, with anti-mining host Palau seating four PIF members engaged in seabed exploration plus rival dialogue partners China and the United States leading the race to the Pacific seabed.
insights.speaker: Oliver Nobetau
insights.so_what: Seabed-mining alignment splits the bloc and pulls in US-China competition — a fault line for critical-minerals supply and Pacific unity.
insights.quote: The prospect of commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific presents an existential challenge to the PIF
insights.locator: The prospect of commercial deep-sea mining

insights.claim: PNG and Solomon Islands will finalise a shared maritime boundary treaty at the Palau meeting, part of a renewed regional push on boundary delimitation since 2021 and 2023 declarations on preserving maritime zones and statehood.
insights.speaker: Oliver Nobetau
insights.so_what: Locking in maritime boundaries secures fisheries and seabed rights as sea levels threaten baselines — relevant to resource and statehood claims.
insights.locator: Pacific nations have pursued outstanding maritime boundary delimitations

insights.claim: Vanuatu's territorial dispute with France over the Matthew and Hunter Islands has been largely unaddressed by the Forum despite PIF's prior involvement in New Caledonia's independence referendums, and Vanuatu intends to elevate the dispute to an international court.
insights.speaker: Oliver Nobetau
insights.so_what: Forum silence on a France dispute while pursuing others signals selective solidarity — watch whether it surfaces in Palau.
insights.quote: Vanuatu’s territorial dispute with France has been largely unaddressed by the Forum

insights.claim: All Forum members are now connected to the global undersea data cable network, with the Lagatoi Declaration's six priority areas and the endorsed Digital Transformation Action Plan raising the question of how the region captures the full economic value of the infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Oliver Nobetau
insights.so_what: Full undersea-cable coverage opens a Pacific digital-economy build-out; implementation and youth digital skills are the gating factors.
insights.locator: Serena Sasingian, FDC Pacific Research Fellow

insights.claim: PIF leaders asked the Secretariat in 2025 to work toward a Forum Leaders' Envoys visit to West Papua in 2026, and PNG Foreign Minister Justin Tkatchenko says West Papua is likely to be discussed in Palau amid continuing human rights concerns over Indonesian sovereignty.
insights.speaker: Oliver Nobetau
insights.so_what: Progress on a West Papua envoy visit is a barometer of PIF-Indonesia trust and of how far human-rights concerns move against a rising development partner.
insights.locator: Indonesia is an ever more active development partner
